subject: The instruction set lags the rules it governs
recordedOccasion: restore-apps session, from its own outstanding items rather than from a fresh reading. Every finding below was noticed by this session while writing Revisions 166 through 173, and deferred in prose at the time.
severity: ** findings F1, F5 and F8 are high. A session that reads only the instruction set does not learn several of the rules it is expected to follow, and one of those rules governs when it may touch the owner's checkout.
scope: ** instruction-set. The fix lands in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` §§4b–4d, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and `docs/architecture/findings-and-sessions.md`.

findings.statement: Five rules exist only in `docs/legend.md` and not in the instruction set
findings.sectionHeading: F1 — five rules exist only in `docs/legend.md`

findings.statement: Two rules exist in both, in different words
findings.sectionHeading: F2 — two rules exist in both, in different words
F3 — §4b's directory list is now wrong

findings.statement: The architecture record describes two findings trees; there are three
findings.sectionHeading: F4 — the architecture record describes two findings trees

findings.statement: Nothing tells a session that `docs/legend.md` is normative
State names and state requirements live in different files
findings.sectionHeading: F6 — state names and state requirements are in different files

findings.statement: The vocabulary cannot say that one bundle must be decided before another
findings.sectionHeading: F7 — the vocabulary cannot express decision order

findings.statement: The rule says where a change is composed, not when it is handed over
findings.sectionHeading: F8 — the rule says where a change is composed, not when it is handed over

findings.statement: Six rules live only in a workspace file, outside the repository entirely
findings.sectionHeading: F9 — six rules live outside the repository entirely

findings.statement: Nothing distinguishes a standing decision from one reopened for re-examination, and no state locks decisions while the work is in flight
findings.sectionHeading: F10 — a decision cannot say it is under re-examination, and nothing locks one

findings.statement: The header schema binds `findings.md` only, and six of eight architecture records render their header as one run-on paragraph
findings.sectionHeading: F11 — the header schema binds one file type, and the records break it

findings.statement: No status transition names the event that triggers it, so a bulk edit moved twenty-one findings and every checker passed
findings.sectionHeading: F12 — a status transition names no trigger, and a sweep is indistinguishable from a reading

decisions.decision: `docs/legend.md` holds VOCABULARY. `.github/copilot-instructions.md` sections 4b–4d hold PROCEDURE. Each points at the other for the kind it does not hold, and the legend is named in §4 as required reading
decisions.sectionHeading: D1 — `docs/legend.md` holds VOCABULARY. `.github/copilot-instructions.md` sections 4b–4d hold PROCEDURE. Each points at the other for the kind it does not hold, and the legend is named in §4 as required reading

decisions.decision: the write categories split. The legend keeps three one-line definitions of what a record, toolkit and evidence write IS. §4b takes the gating
decisions.sectionHeading: D2 — the write categories split. The legend keeps three one-line definitions of what a record, toolkit and evidence write IS. §4b takes the gating

decisions.decision: `docs/INDEX.md` owns the enumeration of the `docs/` directories. §4b and `docs/architecture/findings-and-sessions.md` §2 stop listing them and point at it
decisions.sectionHeading: D3 — `docs/INDEX.md` owns the enumeration of the `docs/` directories. §4b and `docs/architecture/findings-and-sessions.md` §2 stop listing them and point at it

decisions.decision: a bundle waiting on another's decision says so in prose inside its `Relates to` line, and §4c requires the bundle's INDEX.md Notes cell to say it too. `Decide after:` does not become vocabulary
decisions.sectionHeading: D4 — a bundle waiting on another's decision says so in prose inside its `Relates to` line, and §4c requires the bundle's INDEX.md Notes cell to say it too. `Decide after:` does not become vocabulary

decisions.decision: ordering between findings is a typed, directed edge — `blocks` or `evidences` — asserted in the bundle whose session states it, validated at both ends, and expiring when either endpoint goes inert
decisions.sectionHeading: D5 — ordering between findings is a typed, directed edge

decisions.decision: a hand-over step joins the composition rule in section 6: the session reports what it composed and shows it, and the patch is applied only when the owner asks
decisions.sectionHeading: D6 — the hand-over step joins the composition rule in section 6

decisions.decision: A status moves on a **material change to the record**, never on a reading. `reopened` persists until one occurs: a write to the finding or a contribution moves it to `framing`, an accepted decision to `decided`, an executed resolution to `resolved`, and it may be `withdrawn` from there like any live status
decisions.sectionHeading: D7 — a status moves on a material change to the record, never on a reading

decisions.decision: **Reframing a finding invalidates the decisions under it.** One rule, two visible effects: at `decided` the status rolls back to `framing`; at `framing` there is no status to move, so the effect is confined to the decisions. The rollback is the DEFAULT and a session may decline it in writing, recording in `decisions.md` that the edit was non-material and why. `resolved` and `withdrawn` are frozen and unreachable by it
decisions.sectionHeading: D8 — reframing invalidates the decisions under a finding

decisions.decision: A decision's `Outcome` is one of seven — `proposed`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `deferred`, `retracted`, `replaced → DX`, `voided` — and **no word appears in both an Outcome and a status vocabulary**, which a schema check asserts. `refined → DX` and `superseded → DX` collapse into `replaced → DX`
decisions.sectionHeading: D9 — the Outcome vocabulary, and no word in two vocabularies

decisions.decision: **Reopening requires a reason** from a nine-value enumeration, an optional note, `reopened_at`, and the commit SHA at reopen time. The reason determines the exit status rather than leaving it to judgement. `reopened.md` is GENERATED from those fields, never hand-written
decisions.sectionHeading: D10 — reopening takes a reason, and the reason decides the exit

decisions.decision: **Withdrawing requires a reason**, an optional note and `withdrawn_at`, per finding — a bundle-level withdrawal needs one for every finding in it. A `resolved` finding is reopened first; `withdrawn` reaches every status except `resolved`
decisions.sectionHeading: D11 — withdrawing takes a reason too

decisions.decision: **Supersession carries provenance as typed edges at finding granularity, stored in the new bundle only.** `carried`, `successor`, `split`, `merged` and `dropped`; `new` is derived from the absence of an incoming edge. Coverage and exclusivity gate the `superseded` tag. The new bundle gets no `decisions.md`. A superseded bundle is readable by any session and writable by none
decisions.sectionHeading: D12 — supersession carries provenance, at finding granularity

contributions.contribution: Recorded D5 against F7 and set D4's outcome to `superseded → D5`
